interface.signature: def print_next_greater_freq(arr: list[int], n: int) -> list[int]: ...

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in arr) and all(1 <= x <= 10**4 for x in arr) and 1 <= n <= 10**4 and len(arr) == n
preconditions.description: The input array `arr` contains exactly `n` integers, each between 1 and 10^4 inclusive, and `n` is between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(answer) == n and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in answer) and all(-1 <= x <= 10**4 or x == -1 for x in answer)
postconditions.description: The output `answer` is a list of exactly `n` integers, where each element is either -1 or an integer from the input array (1 to 10^4).

postconditions.expression: all((answer[i] == -1 or (answer[i] in arr[i+1:] and (arr.count(answer[i]) > arr.count(arr[i])))) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: For each element `arr[i]` in the input array, `answer[i]` is either -1 (if no such element exists to its right) or the closest element to the right of `arr[i]` whose frequency in the entire array is strictly greater than the frequency of `arr[i]`.

postconditions.expression: all((answer[i] == -1 or (not any(arr.count(x) > arr.count(arr[i]) and x in arr[i+1:j] for j in range(i+2, n+1) for x in arr[i+1:j]))) for i in range(n) if answer[i] != -1)
postconditions.description: If `answer[i]` is not -1, it is the closest element to the right of `arr[i]` with greater frequency, meaning no closer element to the right of `arr[i]` has a greater frequency.
